_README: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE CLIENT ROSTER.
Edit this file, then run `python tools/build-roster.py`. It writes the cards
into site/work/index.html between the two ROSTER markers, and writes
site/assets/js/clients.js for the overlay. Adding a client is one record
here and one command - never hand-edited markup in two places that can
disagree about how many clients there are.
THE HOUSE RULE APPLIES TO EVERY FIELD. null means 'we have not been told',
and renders as a visible [[NEEDS: ...]] on the page. It does NOT mean
'write something plausible'. Every non-null string below is traceable to
reference/reference-sites.md, to brief/04-asset-inventory.md, to the
client's own published site, or to a case page in site/work/.
FIELDS
slug      file-safe id. Must match the _manifest.json key when mark=true.
name      as the client writes it.
sector    the client's own words where they publish them. null if unknown.
cat       the filter shelf. One of the keys in _categories. null = shows
only under Everything, and the roster says so in a note.
band      case | live | mark. Depth of what is on file, not job size.
href      a case page in site/work/, relative. Routes instead of opening
the overlay.
site      the client's live site. null where there is nothing to link.
mark      true when tools/build-client-marks.py has built files for this
slug. false means set initials instead - our setting, which is
honest, where a logo we do not have would not be.
init      the initials to set when mark is false.
line      the one line on the card. null leaves the card short rather
than filling it.
note      an honest caveat shown in place of a link or a figure.
came      what the client came with. The problem, one line.
did       what we did. The approach, one line.
got       what they got. A list of deliverables.
outcome   what happened. [value, label] - or null, or the string
"unpublished", which renders as the qual-note sentence rather
than as a placeholder, because 'the client has not published a
outcome   what happened. [value, label] - or null, or the string
"unpublished", which renders as a sentence rather than a
placeholder, because 'no figure is published for this' is a real
answer and a different one from 'nobody has asked'.
WHERE THE FILLED FIELDS CAME FROM (2026-10-17): each client's own live site,
read directly. `who` and `got` are what they publish about themselves and
what is demonstrably on their site today. `did` is deliberately still null
for every one of them - the approach we took is not on their site and
cannot be read off it, and that is the one line the studio has to supply.

_category_notes.interiors: Four of the twelve are in the built environment: two interior contractors, one fit-out contractor with its own factory, and an acoustics firm. The word each one publishes is on its own card.
_category_notes.velmont: reference/reference-sites.md had Velmont as a 'Design studio'. Its own site says commercial interior contracting, with an in-house manufacturing facility, since 2018. The client's own words win over our internal note.
_category_notes.null: Nuozone Studio and Tulipss publish no sector, so they appear only under Everything rather than being filed under a guess.

clients.name: Zingara
clients.line: It read like three restaurants. One identity across the room, the menu, the packaging and the listings, and a 189-item menu re-set without cutting a dish.

clients.name: The Possah
clients.line: The budget didn’t cover a studio. A full identity and an eleven-section guidelines document, and the collection shot without one.

clients.name: Velmont Design Studio
clients.line: Defining Environments. Fit-outs, furniture and joinery for hotels, hospitals and workplaces, made in their own facility.
clients.came: A Bengaluru contractor since 2018 with its own manufacturing floor, and ITC Ratnadipa in Colombo, Taj Malabar in Kochi and Marriott Marquis in Delhi on the project list. Work at that level has to look like it on a screen, and the site has to carry four disciplines (workplace, healthcare, hospitality and MNC fit-out) without reading as four companies.
clients.did: One site for four disciplines: the project names lead, the portfolio is shown at the standard of the hotels in it, and every page ends at the same enquiry route.
got: The studio, the disciplines and the project portfolio
A four-step process: brief, planning, build, handover

clients.name: Assetly
clients.line: The lighter balance sheet. Operating leases that keep the equipment, and its resale risk, off the customer’s books.
clients.came: A proposition that is hard to say out loud. An operating lease is a tax and balance-sheet argument before it is anything else, and the site has to make that argument to four industries at once: commercial interiors, manufacturing, construction and hospitality.
clients.did: We led with the money. A lease set against buying outright, then a page for each industry, so every reader finds their own case in their own terms.
got: A compare page putting a lease against buying outright
Sector pages for the four industries
Asset categories, from workplace fit-outs to plant and machinery

clients.name: Artizen Projects
clients.line: The Art of Building. Interior fit-outs only: turnkey, general contracting and MEP.
clients.came: A Bangalore firm that does one thing and wants reading as the best at it: 45M sq ft crafted, 50-plus LEED and WELL certified projects, and Telstra, Amazon, Palo Alto Networks, TomTom and WeWork in the clientele. The site has to put those numbers up without sounding like a brochure.
clients.did: We let the record do the talking: the square footage, the certifications and the clientele, set plainly with no brochure voice around them.
got: Know Us, the team and the services
Enquiries and careers on one contact route

clients.name: Noir Velin
clients.line: Drawn. Not generated. Every graphic starts as an original hand drawing.
clients.came: A tee brand whose whole claim is that a person drew it. That claim is worth nothing unless the site proves it, so the drawing has to be the hero rather than the garment, and a drop has to feel like a drop.
clients.did: We made the drawing the hero. Every drop opens on the original art, the garment comes second, and the hand-drawn claim sits on every product page.
got: Drop 01 in five collections: Urban Bird, Anime, Toxic Frogs, Stray Club, Chaos Monkeys
Product pages carrying the hand-drawn and 240 GSM claims
Size chart, FAQs and the policy set

clients.name: Shail Interiors
clients.line: Crafting spaces, inspiring lives. End-to-end contracting for commercial interiors, since 2017.
clients.came: Microsoft, OpenText, IFF, WeWork, HP, GE Appliances, Illumina, Novo Nordisk and Diligent are already on the client list. The job of the site is to make a seven-year-old firm look like the one those names chose.
clients.did: A site built to match the client list: the names up front, the portfolio as the proof, and one clear route to a quote.
got: Our Story, the services and a project portfolio

clients.name: Aware Acoustics
clients.line: Sound shapes how we experience the spaces around us.
clients.note: Our work with Aware Acoustics focuses on translating its technical expertise in architectural acoustics, sound engineering and noise control into a more distinctive digital presence. Through thoughtful design, clear communication and a refined visual direction, the goal is to make complex acoustic solutions easier to understand while building trust with architects, businesses and industry professionals.

clients.name: NUOZONE Boutique
clients.line: A boutique built around craftsmanship, personal expression and the art of dressing for life’s most meaningful occasions.
clients.note: Our work with NUOZONE focuses on elevating its digital presence through thoughtful creative direction, fashion-led storytelling and visually rich content that brings its collections to life. From showcasing intricate details to communicating the experience behind each piece, the goal is to build a more distinctive brand presence that resonates with its audience and turns attention into meaningful customer connections.

clients.name: Tulipss
clients.line: In home textiles, the smallest details often shape how a space feels.
clients.note: Our work with Tulipss centres on translating the comfort, quality and character of its products into a compelling digital brand experience. Through considered visual storytelling, product-focused creative and a cohesive content direction, we aim to present everyday home essentials with greater aspiration and distinction, helping Tulipss connect with modern consumers while building a recognisable identity in a competitive market.

clients.name: Amma’s Breakfast
clients.line: A warm script entirely unlike the parent mark, which is the point of a sub-brand.
